cleansingStrength.rationale: Moderate: C1 pattern - Sodium Laureth Sulfate #2 buffered by Cocamidopropyl Betaine #4 and Cocamide MEA #8 (Sodium Xylenesulfonate #3 is a hydrotrope); late TEA-Dodecylbenzenesulfonate #16 is an emulsion-carrier anionic, not a reinforcing route; no reset intent.
cleansingStrength.counterSignal: 'Classic Clean' and oily-scalp claim; late second anionic.

conditioningLevel.rationale: Moderate: silicone/cationic system (Dimethiconol #11, Guar Hydroxypropyltrimonium Chloride #13, Dimethicone #14) plus pearlizer Glycol Distearate #9; humectants are late (Glycerin #23, Panthenol #25). Silicones follow Parfum, so the C2 'early silicone' condition is not clearly met.
conditioningLevel.counterSignal: Silicone + cationic + pearlizer + humectants resembles the C2 high pattern.

weightPotential.rationale: Moderate: silicone/guar coacervate deposition (#11, #13, #14) plus pearlizer #9 is one persistent system bounded by an effective SLES/betaine base; not a rich 2-in-1 (W1 analogue).
weightPotential.whyNotNeighborBand: Not high: single route kind with effective reset. Low is the realistic neighbor (silicones after Parfum).

focusPrimary.rationale: scalp_active: problem-led anti-dandruff product ('Anti-Schuppen' in name) with recognized active Piroctone Olamine #10 (7.2).
focusPrimary.decisionTrace: Blind: recognized active -> scalp_active compatible. Unblind: anti-dandruff name -> scalp_active.

focusSecondary.rationale: Empty: the oily-scalp and itch claims are part of the same scalp_active '3X' positioning; a clarifying secondary would need compatible oily-root/reset architecture, which a C1 moderate chassis with silicone deposition does not provide.

usageRole.rationale: Treatment: supported anti-dandruff formula with problem-led positioning (§9). The frequent trigger is also met ('ideal für die tägliche Anwendung', cleansing not strong); treatment chosen as the more specific product-level role.

scalpComfortTarget.rationale: Not targeted: itch is claimed only as 'Juckreiz im Zusammenhang mit Schuppen' (a dandruff symptom), and the formula lacks a supportive comfort architecture - comfort/humectant routes are late (Glycerin #23, Niacinamide #24, Panthenol #25), fragrance is prominent (#6), plus dyes.

projection.thicknessRationale: T1 W moderate, C moderate: fine acceptable, normal ideal, coarse acceptable; scalp-concern targets, T6 has nothing to lift. T4: W neighbor low keeps normal ideal and raises fine; C neighbor high raises coarse -> no flags.
projection.scalpTargetRationale: S-DANDRUFF: 'Anti-Schuppen' in name (E1 high) + supported -> pass (primary by S-PRIMARY). S-OILY: E2 'fettige Kopfhaut' as a named problem on the exact manufacturer page (E1 moderate); formula: cleansing moderate, W moderate (not high), C moderate (not high) -> pass; distinct claim and own gate -> secondary (S-SECONDARY; dandruff+oily not prohibited). S-SENSITIVE: E2 'Juckreiz' present but scalpComfortTarget not_targeted -> gate fails; S-FAIL not triggered because another specialist target qualifies. S-FOCUS: scalp_active -> no mismatch (oily is not in the S-FOCUS list).
projection.cleansingIntensityRationale: I1: moderate -> regular; equals both schuppen and dehydriert-fettig expectations. I3: no neighbor.
projection.liveComparison: Not evaluated (live rows not in sealed packet).

uncertainties: §9 has no precedence when both 'frequent' (daily-use + not strong) and 'treatment' (supported anti-dandruff) triggers are met; chose treatment.

S-SECONDARY permits an oily secondary on an anti-dandruff product when the oily-scalp problem is one bullet of a multi-problem claim; the standard does not say whether such a bundled claim counts as a 'distinct' E2 claim. Applied literally -> oily secondary, which adds three rows (recommending direction).
Itch claimed as a dandruff symptom ('Juckreiz im Zusammenhang mit Schuppen'): whether this is sensitive-scalp positioning under §10/E2 is not specified.
S-FOCUS lists only dandruff/sensitive/dry; an oily target never checks focus consistency.
